sentences.text: Der var engang en soldat, som kom hjem fra krigen.
sentences.translation: Once upon a time there was a soldier who came home from the war.

words.grammar: en soldat · soldaten (the soldier) · soldater (plural)
en krig · krigen (the war) · fra krigen = from the war

sentences.text: På vejen mødte han en gammel heks.
sentences.translation: On the way he met an old witch.

words.grammar: møde (to meet) · mødte (past) · har mødt (perfect) · weak verb
en heks · heksen (the witch) · hekse (plural)

sentences.text: Heksen sagde: "Gå ned i træet, og hent mit fyrtøj."
sentences.translation: The witch said: "Climb down into the tree, and fetch my tinderbox."

words.grammar: hente (to fetch) · imperative: hent · hente noget = to go and get something
et fyrtøj · fyrtøjet (the tinderbox) · an old tool for lighting fire

sentences.text: Soldaten gik ned og fandt mange guldmønter.
sentences.translation: The soldier climbed down and found many gold coins.

words.grammar: finde (to find) · fandt (past) · har fundet (perfect) · strong verb
en guldmønt · guldmønter (plural) · compound: guld (gold) + mønt (coin)

sentences.text: Han tog guldet og fyrtøjet med op.
sentences.translation: He took the gold and the tinderbox up with him.

words.grammar: tage (to take) · tog (past) · har taget (perfect) · strong verb
med = along, with · op = up · together: brought it up with him

sentences.text: Men heksen ville ikke sige, hvorfor fyrtøjet var vigtigt.
sentences.translation: But the witch would not say why the tinderbox was important.

words.grammar: ville (modal: want to/would) · present: vil · ville ikke = refused to
vigtig (common) · vigtigt (neuter) · agrees with fyrtøjet (et-word)

sentences.text: Soldaten blev vred og gik videre med fyrtøjet.
sentences.translation: The soldier became angry and went on with the tinderbox.

words.grammar: blive (to become) · blev (past) · er blevet (perfect) · blev vred = became angry
vred (common) · vredt (neuter) · vrede (pl./def.)

sentences.text: I byen levede han som en rig mand.
sentences.translation: In the town he lived like a rich man.

words.grammar: leve (to live) · levede (past) · har levet (perfect) · weak verb
rig (common) · rigt (neuter) · rige (pl./def.)

sentences.text: En dag slog han på fyrtøjet, og en stor hund kom frem.
sentences.translation: One day he struck the tinderbox, and a big dog appeared.

words.grammar: slå (to strike) · slog (past) · har slået (perfect) · strong verb
komme frem = to come forward / appear · komme (past: kom) + frem (forward)

sentences.text: Hunden kunne give ham alt, hvad han ønskede.
sentences.translation: The dog could give him anything he wished for.

words.grammar: kunne (modal: can) · past of kan · kunne give = could give
ønske (to wish) · ønskede (past) · har ønsket (perfect) · weak verb

sentences.text: Soldaten brugte hunden til at møde en smuk prinsesse.
sentences.translation: The soldier used the dog to meet a beautiful princess.

words.grammar: bruge (to use) · brugte (past) · har brugt (perfect) · weak verb
smuk (common) · smukt (neuter) · smukke (pl./def.)

sentences.text: De blev gift, og soldaten blev konge.
sentences.translation: They got married, and the soldier became king.

words.grammar: blive gift = to get married · være gift = to be married · blive signals the change of state
en konge · kongen (the king) · konger (plural)

metadata.adaptedFrom: Adapted from H.C. Andersen, Fyrtøjet (1835), simplified for A1 learners

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Der var engang en soldat, som kom hjem fra krigen.
grammarPoints.explanation: Just like "Prinsessen på ærten", this story opens with the fixed phrase "Der var engang" (once upon a time), using the past tense of være (var) and the dummy subject der.

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Soldaten blev vred. / Soldaten blev konge.
grammarPoints.explanation: Blive marks a change of state — going from not-angry to angry, or from soldier to king. Compare være, which describes an existing state without any change.

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Hunden kunne give ham alt, hvad han ønskede.
grammarPoints.explanation: Kunne is the past tense of kan (can) and expresses what someone was able to do. Like other modal verbs, it is followed directly by an infinitive with no "at": kunne give, not kunne at give.
